senses.def: having passed the exams or training needed for a job
ex: She is a qualified nurse.
We need fully qualified teachers.

senses.def: not complete or total; with some conditions
ex: The film received qualified praise from critics.

senses.def: to pass the exams or training needed to do a job
ex: He qualified as a doctor in 2018.
It takes five years to qualify.

senses.def: to have the right to do or receive something
ex: Children under five qualify for free travel.

senses.def: to reach the next part of a competition
ex: Our team qualified for the final.

mistake.note: Use 'qualify as' + a job, and 'qualify for' + a prize or right.

senses.def: how good or bad something is
ex: The quality of the food was excellent.
This shop sells good quality clothes.

senses.def: a feature of a person or thing, especially a good one
ex: Honesty is a quality I admire.

senses.def: of a very good standard
ex: We offer quality products at low prices.

senses.def: a period when a person or animal is kept apart so a disease cannot spread
ex: Travellers must stay in quarantine for ten days.
The dog was kept in quarantine.

senses.def: an angry argument between people
ex: She had a quarrel with her sister.
It started as a small quarrel.

senses.def: to have an angry argument
ex: The two brothers quarrelled over money.

senses.def: a place where stone or sand is dug out of the ground
ex: Stone from the quarry was used to build the church.

senses.def: a person or animal that is being hunted
ex: The hunters followed their quarry through the forest.

senses.def: a woman who rules a country, or the wife of a king
ex: The queen waved to the crowd.
She became queen at the age of twenty.

senses.def: a playing card or chess piece with a queen's picture or powers
ex: He lost his queen early in the chess game.

senses.def: strange or unusual, in an old-fashioned use
ex: There was a queer smell in the room.

senses.def: a long search for something difficult to find or achieve
ex: She went on a quest for the truth.
His quest for fame lasted years.

senses.def: a sentence that asks for an answer
ex: Can I ask you a question?
She answered all my questions.

senses.def: a matter that needs to be discussed or decided
ex: The question is how we pay for it.

senses.def: a feeling of doubt about something
ex: There is no question that she is talented.

senses.def: to ask someone questions, especially officially
ex: Police questioned him for three hours.

senses.def: to feel doubt about something
ex: I never questioned her honesty.

mistake.note: We say 'ask a question', not 'make a question' (influence of Arabic طرح سؤالاً).

senses.def: a line of people waiting for something, one behind the other
ex: There was a long queue outside the cinema.
We joined the queue for tickets.

senses.def: to wait in a line for something
ex: People queued for hours to see the show.

senses.def: done or happening in a short time
ex: Let's take a quick break.
She gave a quick answer.

senses.def: able to learn or react fast
ex: He is quick at maths.

senses.def: in a way that makes little or no noise
ex: She closed the door quietly.
He spoke quietly to the baby.

senses.def: in a calm way without drawing attention
ex: He quietly left the meeting.

senses.def: unusual in an interesting or charming way
ex: The cafe has a quirky sense of humour.
She wore quirky hats.

senses.def: unusual in an interesting or charming way
ex: Everyone loves the quirky little bookshop.

senses.def: to leave a job or school
ex: He quit his job last month.
She quit school at sixteen.

senses.def: to stop doing something
ex: He quit smoking two years ago.

senses.def: free of something unpleasant
ex: We are glad to be quit of the problem.

senses.def: to a fairly large degree but not extremely
ex: The film was quite good.
It's quite cold today.

senses.def: completely
ex: I'm not quite ready yet.
That is quite impossible.

senses.def: to shake slightly, especially because of fear or strong feeling
ex: Her voice quivered with anger.

senses.def: a small shaking movement
ex: He felt a quiver of excitement.

senses.def: a group of words taken from a book or speech
ex: The essay begins with a quote from Shakespeare.

senses.def: a statement of how much a job will cost
ex: We got three quotes for the repair.

senses.def: to repeat the exact words that someone else wrote or said
ex: She quoted a line from the poem.
Please don't quote me on that.
